note: The half that sailed from Port Hueneme on 6 Oct 1942 (the rolls' "Sec 2"); reunited with the second wave at Nouméa on 13 Dec 1942 (ncbhist-020/p2).
The half that stayed at Port Hueneme until 26 Nov 1942 (the rolls' "Section 1") (ncbhist-020/p2).
About 500 men: Townsville, Woodlark, Kiriwina, Milne Bay, Brisbane; the 1st Section from October 1943 (ncbhist-020/p2-p3).
The rest: Guadalcanal, the Russells, New Georgia, then Banika; the 2nd Section, its rolls headed "Detachment" and "Second Section" (ncbhist-020/p2-p3).

About 400 men (12 officers, 403 men; 1 1/2 companies) under Lt. Riordan at Oloana Bay, Vangunu (ncbhist-020/p2, p11; mcsol ch. 2). Its first echelon (3 officers, 114 men) left for Bau Island on 9 September 1943, its second (10 officers, 262 men) for Ondonga on 9 and 15 October (ncbhist-020/p11-p12).

About 140 men (3 officers, 142 men; one company) under Lt. Sanders at Viru Harbor (ncbhist-020/p2, p11); left in echelons on 5-9 September 1943 for East Rovianna and Doke Doke, and from East Rovianna for Bau Island, arriving 5 November (ncbhist-020/p11-p12).

The PT-boat base on Bau Island, Rendova Harbor: Group One's first echelon from 10 September 1943, joined by the Viru company on 5 November; 4 officers and 211 men left for the Russells on 9 January 1944 (ncbhist-020/p11-p12).
23 officers and 749 men, Saipan to Okinawa in four LSTs, 12-17 April 1945 (ncbhist-020/p12; LST-824 and LST-898 war diaries).
4 officers and 276-277 men, on Saipan until 7 May 1945; joined the first echelon on Okinawa on 14 May (ncbhist-020/p12, p5).
